verification.note: The previous MISMATCH note was WRONG. It read the API signature -- months_ahead: Query(18, ge=3, le=36) -- and concluded the range was 3-36. Both UIs offer exactly 6/12/18/24/36, so the user-facing range really is 6-36 and the copy's figures were always correct. The real inaccuracy was subtler: months_ahead is a lookahead CAP, not a band (m_away <= months_ahead), so 'expiring in 6-36 months' implies a floor that does not exist -- 'Next 6 months' includes a contract ending next month. Reworded to 'the next 6 to 36 months', matching the UI's own 'Next N months' labels and the KB's 'hard cap' wording. 'Zero AI credits' holds: the endpoint docstring is 'No AI calls, no tier gate -- pure data analysis over public USASpending records.'

topics.headline: Built-in FAR 52.219-14 compliance check.
topics.body: Model your prime/sub split for a compliant / at-risk / over-limit verdict — evaluated across the base period AND each option year, since a plan can pass on total dollars yet fail a single year.
topics.hook_x: A subcontracting plan can pass on total dollars and still fail a single option year. PursuitAI's FAR 52.219-14 calculator checks every period separately — and tells you exactly how much headroom you have left.
topics.hook_ig:
The Limitations on Subcontracting rule (FAR 52.219-14) kills more set-aside bids than bad pricing.

PursuitAI models your prime/sub split — counting similarly-situated entities correctly — for a compliant / at-risk / over-limit verdict BEFORE you sign. Evaluated across the base period and every option year separately.

A dollar-headroom solver even tells you which partner to adjust to recover the most room.

verification.note: 50% for services and supplies; similarly-situated entities excluded. The clause also sets 85%/75% construction limits the '50% Rule' shorthand elides.

angles.headline: Passes on total dollars. Fails in year three.
angles.body: A teaming split can satisfy the limitation across the whole contract and still breach it inside a single option year. Every year is evaluated on its own.
angles.hook_x: A prime/sub split can pass the limitation on total contract dollars and still fail inside one option year. PursuitAI evaluates the base period and every option year separately, so the breach shows up before you sign.
angles.hook_ig:
Here is the trap in the limitation on subcontracting.

Your split can be comfortably compliant across the whole contract value — and still breach in option year three, where the work mix shifts.

Every period gets evaluated on its own: base, and each option year, with a compliant / at-risk / over-limit verdict for each.
